Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move ahead with Redwood for our inference layer. We have a product launch window that will generate a significant spike in traffic over the first 6–12 weeks. To proceed with procurement we need two exceptions in the SLA template before legal/finance can approve a PO: 

1) A temporary uptime uplift to 99.99% for the first 90 days post-go-live (we're currently comfortable with Redwood's standard baseline but need tighter guarantees during launch).
2) A monthly service-credit ladder that scales more generously for the launch period (credits anchored to observed downtime per 14-day buckets rather than a single 30-day window).

I attached our standard procurement template for reference (fastmed_procurement_template.pdf). Can Redwood provide an outline of how the credits would calculate and whether there's a feasible operational carveout for planned maintenance during the peak? Also, we need a clear SLA measurement cadence so our ops team can align monitoring.

Appreciate a quick turn — we are hoping to finalize commercial paperwork by the end of next week.

Best,

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.ai>

Team — forwarding FastMed's ask. Key asks: temporary 99.99% uplift for 90 days and a more generous, short-window monthly credit ladder (they propose 14-day buckets for the launch). Quick thoughts and recommended approach below.

Proposed commercial/ops compromise:
- Temporary uplift: agree to 99.99% for a 90-day "launch window" if customer commits to a minimum reserved capacity slot (Dedicated or Reserved Burst) for the period. This avoids exposing hosted capacity and keeps predictable economics.
- Credit ladder: calculate credits on rolling 14-day measurement windows for the launch period only; after the 90 days revert to our standard 30-day measurement window. Credits capped at a single month of committed spend (cap protects Redwood).
- Maintenance carveouts: standard planned maintenance windows will be assessed but offer an extended notification requirement (72 hours) for launch period; mission-critical emergency maintenance must be coordinated via our on-call to minimize impact.
- Measurement & reporting: we will provide token-level latency/uptime export and an ops dashboard share; measurement will be based on per-region availability with aggregation rules (we can draft the exact formula).

Action items: 
- Ben: Draft a short SLA amendment (redwood_sla_draft_v2.pdf) with the uplift clause, 14-day ladder for 90 days, cap language, and maintenance carveouts.
- Markus: Legal to validate the cap + measurement wording and confirm DocuSign flow.
- Marissa: Confirm pricing/commitment asks for Reserved capacity and a failback plan if dedicated slots are unavailable.

If we sign off internally, I can push the redline to FastMed and request a DocuSign envelope. I recommend we avoid permanent baseline changes — make this a time-boxed amendment tied to their launch.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Redwood Inference
